models_evaluated: FDA De Novo cleared autonomous AI for diabetic eye disease testing

links.outcome: Change in diabetic eye disease testing adherence by race at AI vs non-AI sites
links.effect: Black/African American adherence rose 11.9% at AI-switched sites vs fell 1.2% at non-AI sites; Asian vs Black gap shrank from 15.6% (61.1% vs 45.5%) to 3.5% by 2021.
links.quote: The adherence rate for Black/African Americans increased by 11.9% within AI-switched sites whereas it decreased by 1.2% within non-AI sites over the same time frame.

links.outcome: Racial disparities in adherence to annual diabetic eye disease testing
links.effect: The Asian American–Black/African American adherence gap narrowed from 15.6% in 2019 (61.1% vs. 45.5%) to 3.5% by 2021, indicating reduced but persistent disparity.

unlisted_practices: Provide autonomous AI diabetic eye disease testing in primary care rather than relying only on referrals to eyecare.

links.effect: The odds ratio of adherence at AI-switched sites was 36% higher than at non-AI sites.
links.quote: First, after controlling for a wide range of potential confounders, our regression analysis demonstrated that the odds ratio of adherence at AI-switched sites was 36% higher than that of non-AI sites, suggesting that there was a higher increase in DED testing between 2019 and 2021 at AI-switched sites than at non-AI sites.

links.effect: The 15.6% adherence gap between Asian Americans and Black/African Americans shrank to 3.5%.
